---
title: "Ex - GroupBy (Alcohol Consumption) - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

### Introduction:

GroupBy can be summarized as Split-Apply-Combine. In dplyr this is
`group_by()` + `summarise()`.

Special thanks to: https://github.com/justmarkham for sharing the dataset and materials.

Check out this [Diagram](http://i.imgur.com/yjNkiwL.png)

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justmarkham/DAT8/master/data/drinks.csv).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called drinks. (Watch the values of the column continent: NA means North America, and look at how R interprets it!)

```{r}
# by default read_csv() turns the text "NA" into a missing value,
# so North America would disappear. na = character() disables that.
drinks <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justmarkham/DAT8/master/data/drinks.csv",
                   na = character())
head(drinks)
```

### Step 4. Which continent drinks more beer on average?

```{r}
drinks |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(beer_servings = mean(beer_servings)) |>
  arrange(desc(beer_servings))
```

### Step 5. For each continent print the statistics for wine consumption.

```{r}
drinks |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(count = n(),
            mean = mean(wine_servings),
            std = sd(wine_servings),
            min = min(wine_servings),
            `25%` = quantile(wine_servings, 0.25),
            `50%` = median(wine_servings),
            `75%` = quantile(wine_servings, 0.75),
            max = max(wine_servings))
```

### Step 6. Print the mean alcohol consumption per continent for every column

```{r}
drinks |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), mean))
```

### Step 7. Print the median alcohol consumption per continent for every column

```{r}
drinks |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), median))
```

### Step 8. Print the mean, min and max values for spirit consumption for each Continent.

#### This time output a DataFrame

```{r}
drinks |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(spirit_servings),
            min = min(spirit_servings),
            max = max(spirit_servings))
```
